headline: A 2022 law lets Justice Department opioid grants fund pilot programs in rural areas, including alternatives to jail, aimed at reducing overdose deaths.
what_it_does: The law expands what money from the Comprehensive Opioid, Stimulant, and Substance Abuse Program can be used for. Grants administered by the Department of Justice may now pay for pilot programs in rural areas. These programs are meant to set up community responses focused on reducing opioid overdose deaths. The programs may include alternatives to incarceration.

who_it_affects.how: Local governments and community groups in rural areas may be able to apply for grant money to run pilot overdose-response programs.

who_it_affects.group: People with opioid addiction in rural areas
who_it_affects.how: Residents who struggle with opioid use in rural areas could see new community programs, and some of these may offer alternatives to jail.

who_it_affects.group: Law enforcement and courts in rural areas
who_it_affects.how: Local police, courts, and jails may see new options that steer some people toward treatment or community programs instead of incarceration.
